The molecule contains an amine nitrogen and a hydroxyl group, allowing for strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding (O-H...N). This interaction is the dominant stabilizing factor across the conformers. I calculated approximate O...N and H...N distances for each structure to quantify H-bond strength. Conformers with H...N distances between 1.9-2.4 Å and O...N distances of 2.5-2.8 Å form tight, favorable pseudo-rings, significantly lowering their energy. These are ranked highest (e.g., 19, 4, 15, 20, 22, 8, 13, 30). 

Conformers with moderate H-bonds (H...N ~2.5-2.7 Å) or slightly distorted geometries that reduce linearity fall into the middle tier (e.g., 1, 27, 6, 23, 21, 12, 17, 5, 25, 3, 7, 28). Some mid-tier structures like 16 show very short O...N distances but suboptimal H alignment, suggesting steric folding rather than optimal H-bonding.

The least stable conformers lack any hydrogen bond entirely (O...N > 3.3 Å) or are highly extended/strained with no compensating interactions. These suffer from lost stabilizing electrostatic energy and potential steric clashes between distant chain ends or eclipsed heavy-atom torsions. They are placed at the bottom (e.g., 9, 11, 2, 14, 10, 24, 26, 29, 18). Uncertainty remains regarding precise van der Waals repulsion and solvent effects, but geometric H-bond proximity reliably predicts relative gas-phase stability ordering for this dataset.
